lessons.title: DOM Manipulation
lessons.html:
DOM Manipulation Fundamentals

The Document Object Model (DOM) represents HTML as a tree structure. JavaScript can read/modify this tree dynamically without page reload.

Selecting Elements:

  • document.getElementById('id') - By ID (fastest)
  • document.querySelector('.class') - First match CSS selector
  • document.querySelectorAll('tag') - All matches
<button id="myBtn">Click me</button>
<div id="output"></div>
const btn = document.getElementById('myBtn');
const output = document.getElementById('output');

btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    output.textContent = 'Button clicked!';
    output.style.color = 'blue';
    output.style.fontSize = '20px';
});

Practice: Create counter button that changes background color randomly.

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

ES6+ JavaScript Features

// Old way
function add(a, b) {
    return a + b;

const person = { name: 'Alice', age: 30, city: 'NY' };

lessons.title: Async JavaScript
lessons.html:
Asynchronous Programming

JavaScript handles async operations with Promises and async/await. Perfect for API calls.

Fetch API + Promises:

fetch('https://api.github.com/users/octocat')
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(user => {
    document.body.innerHTML += `<h2>${user.name}</h2><p>${user.bio}</p>`;
  })
  .catch(error => console.error('Error:', error));

Cleaner async/await:

async function getUser() {
    try {
        const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/users/octocat');
        const user = await response.json();
        console.log(`${user.login} - ${user.public_repos} repos`);
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Failed to fetch user');
    }
}

class TodoApp {

    addTask(text) {
        this.todos.push({
            id: Date.now(),

            completed: false,

lessons.title: Fetch API & HTTP Requests
lessons.html:
Making HTTP Requests

The Fetch API provides a modern interface for making HTTP requests from the browser.

GET Requests:

async function getUsers() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/users', {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: {
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${getToken()}`
      }
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const users = await response.json();
    return users;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to fetch users:', error);
    throw error;
  }
}

POST and Other Methods:

async function createUser(userData) {
  const response = await fetch('/api/users', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(userData),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const error = await response.json();
    throw new Error(error.message || 'Failed to create user');
  }

  return await response.json();
}

// PUT request
async function updateUser(id, userData) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'PUT',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(userData),
  });
  return await response.json();
}

// DELETE request
async function deleteUser(id) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
  });
  return response.status === 204;  // No content
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a REST client with all CRUD operations
  2. Add request retry logic for network failures
  3. Implement request cancellation with AbortController

Key Takeaways:

  • Fetch returns a Promise that resolves to Response
  • Always check response.ok before parsing body
  • Errors should be caught and handled gracefully

lessons.title: CSS Animations & Transitions
lessons.html:
CSS Animations and Transitions

CSS animations bring web pages to life with smooth transitions and keyframe animations.

CSS Transitions:

/* Transition: property duration easing-function delay */
.button {
  background-color: blue;
  color: white;
  padding: 10px 20px;
  transition: background-color 0.3s ease, transform 0.2s ease;
}

.button:hover {
  background-color: darkblue;
  transform: scale(1.05);
}

/* Fade in */
.modal {
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out;
}

.modal.active {
  opacity: 1;
}

/* Slide down */
.dropdown {
  max-height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: max-height 0.3s ease-out;
}

.dropdown.open {
  max-height: 500px;
}

Keyframe Animations:

@keyframes slideIn {
  from {
    transform: translateX(-100%);
    opacity: 0;
  }
  to {
    transform: translateX(0);
    opacity: 1;
  }
}

@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% {
    transform: scale(1);
  }
  50% {
    transform: scale(1.1);
  }
}

@keyframes spin {
  0% { transform: rotate(0deg); }
  100% { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}

.animated-element {
  animation: slideIn 0.5s ease-out forwards;
}

.loader {
  width: 40px;
  height: 40px;
  border: 4px solid #f3f3f3;
  border-top: 4px solid blue;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin 1s linear infinite;
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a fade-in page transition effect
  2. Build a loading spinner component
  3. Implement a slide-in notification system

Key Takeaways:

  • Transitions smooth property changes over time
  • Keyframes define multi-step animations
  • GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity) perform best

lessons.title: Responsive Design & Media Queries
lessons.html:
Building Responsive Websites

Responsive design ensures websites work on all devices. Media queries adjust styles based on viewport size.

Mobile-First CSS:

/* Base styles (mobile first) */
.container {
  padding: 10px;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 10px;
}

.nav {
  display: none;  /* Hidden on mobile */
}

.hamburger {
  display: block;
}

/* Tablet (768px+) */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .container {
    flex-direction: row;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    max-width: 720px;
    margin: 0 auto;
  }

  .nav {
    display: flex;
    gap: 20px;
  }

  .hamburger {
    display: none;
  }
}

/* Desktop (1024px+) */
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .container {
    max-width: 960px;
    padding: 20px;
  }

  .grid {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
    gap: 20px;
  }
}

/* Large desktop (1440px+) */
@media (min-width: 1440px) {
  .container {
    max-width: 1200px;
  }
}

Responsive Images:

<img src="photo-800.jpg"
     srcset="photo-400.jpg 400w,
             photo-800.jpg 800w,
             photo-1200.jpg 1200w"
     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 400px,
            (max-width: 1200px) 800px,
            1200px"
     alt="Responsive image">

<picture>
  <source media="(min-width: 1024px)" srcset="hero-large.jpg">
  <source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset="hero-medium.jpg">
  <img src="hero-small.jpg" alt="Hero image">
</picture>

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a mobile-first responsive navigation
  2. Build a responsive card grid that adapts to screen size
  3. Add responsive images with srcset

Key Takeaways:

  • Design mobile-first, then enhance for larger screens
  • Media queries adapt layout to viewport
  • Responsive images save bandwidth on mobile

lessons.title: Browser Storage & IndexedDB
lessons.html:
Client-Side Data Storage

IndexedDB provides a NoSQL database in the browser for complex offline data.

IndexedDB Basics:

const dbName = 'MyAppDB';
const dbVersion = 1;

function openDB() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = indexedDB.open(dbName, dbVersion);

    request.onupgradeneeded = (event) => {
      const db = event.target.result;

      // Create object stores
      if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('users')) {
        const store = db.createObjectStore('users', {
          keyPath: 'id',
          autoIncrement: true,
        });
        store.createIndex('email', 'email', { unique: true });
        store.createIndex('name', 'name', { unique: false });
      }

      if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains('notes')) {
        const store = db.createObjectStore('notes', {
          keyPath: 'id',
        });
        store.createIndex('userId', 'userId', { unique: false });
      }
    };

    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

CRUD Operations:

async function addUser(user) {
  const db = await openDB();
  const tx = db.transaction('users', 'readwrite');
  const store = tx.objectStore('users');

  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = store.add(user);
    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

async function getUsers() {
  const db = await openDB();
  const tx = db.transaction('users', 'readonly');
  const store = tx.objectStore('users');

  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = store.getAll();
    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

async function searchByEmail(email) {
  const db = await openDB();
  const tx = db.transaction('users', 'readonly');
  const store = tx.objectStore('users');
  const index = store.index('email');

  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = index.get(email);
    request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
    request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
  });
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build an offline-capable note-taking app
  2. Implement data sync between IndexedDB and server
  3. Create a caching layer with IndexedDB for API responses

Key Takeaways:

  • IndexedDB stores structured data in the browser
  • Indexes enable efficient querying
  • Transactions ensure data consistency

lessons.title: Design Patterns in JavaScript
lessons.html:
Common JavaScript Patterns

Design patterns solve common problems in web development. JavaScript's dynamic nature makes some patterns simpler.

Module Pattern:

// Revealing Module Pattern
const UserModule = (function() {
  // Private members
  let userCount = 0;
  const users = [];

  function validateEmail(email) {
    return email.includes('@');
  }

  function generateId() {
    return Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).substr(2);
  }

  // Public API
  return {
    addUser(name, email) {
      if (!validateEmail(email)) {
        throw new Error('Invalid email');
      }
      const user = { id: generateId(), name, email };
      users.push(user);
      userCount++;
      return user;
    },

    getUsers() {
      return [...users];
    },

    getUserCount() {
      return userCount;
    },

    removeUser(id) {
      const index = users.findIndex(u => u.id === id);
      if (index !== -1) {
        users.splice(index, 1);
        userCount--;
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    }
  };
})();

Observer Pattern (Event Emitter):

class EventEmitter {
  constructor() {
    this.handlers = new Map();
  }

  on(event, handler) {
    if (!this.handlers.has(event)) {
      this.handlers.set(event, new Set());
    }
    this.handlers.get(event).add(handler);
    return () => this.off(event, handler);  // Return unsubscribe function
  }

  off(event, handler) {
    this.handlers.get(event)?.delete(handler);
  }

  emit(event, ...args) {
    this.handlers.get(event)?.forEach(handler => {
      handler(...args);
    });
  }

  once(event, handler) {
    const wrapper = (...args) => {
      handler(...args);
      this.off(event, wrapper);
    };
    this.on(event, wrapper);
  }
}

// Usage
const bus = new EventEmitter();
const unsub = bus.on('user:created', user => console.log('User created:', user));
bus.emit('user:created', { name: 'Alice' });
unsub();  // Unsubscribe

Practice Exercises:

  1. Implement a singleton cache manager
  2. Build a pub/sub event bus for component communication
  3. Create a factory for generating form field components

Key Takeaways:

  • Module pattern provides encapsulation
  • Observer pattern enables decoupled communication
  • Factory pattern abstracts object creation

lessons.title: Web Components
lessons.html:
Building Custom HTML Elements

Web Components let you create custom HTML elements with encapsulated styles and behavior.

Custom Element:

class UserCard extends HTMLElement {

    this.render();

lessons.title: Single Page Application
lessons.html:
Building a SPA from Scratch

Single Page Applications handle routing and rendering client-side without full page reloads.

Simple Router:

class Router {
  constructor(routes) {
    this.routes = routes;
    this.currentRoute = null;

    window.addEventListener('popstate', () => this.handleRoute());
    document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      const link = e.target.closest('a[data-link]');
      if (link) {
        e.preventDefault();
        this.navigate(link.href);
      }
    });
  }

  navigate(url) {
    history.pushState(null, '', url);
    this.handleRoute();
  }

  async handleRoute() {
    const path = window.location.pathname;

    // Find matching route
    for (const [pattern, handler] of Object.entries(this.routes)) {
      const params = this.matchRoute(pattern, path);
      if (params !== null) {
        if (this.currentRoute) {
          this.currentRoute.unmount?.();
        }

        const component = await handler(params);
        this.renderComponent(component);
        this.currentRoute = component;
        return;
      }
    }

    // 404
    this.renderComponent({ render: () => '
404 - Page Not Found
' });
  }

  matchRoute(pattern, path) {
    const regexStr = pattern
      .replace(/:([^/]+)/g, '(?<$1>[^/]+)')
      .replace(/\//g, '\\/');
    const regex = new RegExp(`^${regexStr}$`);
    const match = path.match(regex);
    return match ? match.groups : null;
  }

  renderComponent(component) {
    const app = document.getElementById('app');
    app.innerHTML = '';
    const element = component.render();
    if (typeof element === 'string') {
      app.innerHTML = element;
    } else {
      app.appendChild(element);
    }
    component.mounted?.();
  }
}

Usage:

const routes = {
  '/': () => import('./pages/Home.js'),
  '/users': () => import('./pages/Users.js'),
  '/users/:id': (params) => import('./pages/UserProfile.js')
    .then(m => m.default(params)),
  '/about': () => import('./pages/About.js'),
};

const router = new Router(routes);
router.navigate('/');  // Start

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a SPA with lazy-loaded route components
  2. Add route guards for authentication
  3. Implement transition animations between routes

Key Takeaways:

  • History API manages URL without page reload
  • Dynamic imports enable code splitting
  • Client-side routing creates smooth UX

lessons.title: Progressive Web Apps
lessons.html:
Building Offline-Ready Web Apps

PWAs provide an app-like experience with offline support, push notifications, and home screen installation.

Service Worker:

// sw.js
const CACHE_NAME = 'my-pwa-v1';
const ASSETS = [
  '/',
  '/index.html',
  '/styles.css',
  '/app.js',
  '/manifest.json',
  '/icons/icon-192.png',
  '/icons/icon-512.png',
];

// Install event - cache app shell
self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_NAME)
      .then(cache => cache.addAll(ASSETS))
      .then(() => self.skipWaiting())
  );
});

// Activate event - clean old caches
self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then(keys =>
      Promise.all(keys.map(key => {
        if (key !== CACHE_NAME) {
          return caches.delete(key);
        }
      }))
    ).then(() => self.clients.claim())
  );
});

// Fetch event - serve from cache, fallback to network
self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(event.request)
      .then(cached => {
        if (cached) {
          return cached;  // Cache first
        }

        return fetch(event.request)
          .then(response => {
            // Cache new resources
            return caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then(cache => {
              cache.put(event.request, response.clone());
              return response;
            });
          })
          .catch(() => {
            // Offline fallback
            if (event.request.mode === 'navigate') {
              return caches.match('/offline.html');
            }
          });
      })
  );
});

Web App Manifest:

  "name": "My Progressive App",
  "short_name": "MyApp",
